title: Console usage admission controller and schema governor
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Console backend emits high-volume usage events (route hits, token costs, rollout signals). Downstream analytics and billing consumers are fragile to schema drift: missing fields, nested shape changes, and silent typing differences cause partial failures, hidden data loss, and costly debugging. We also see bursts of malformed events from SDK clients and experimental features that increase validation load.

Goal: Build a resilient "admission controller" microservice that sits at the usage event ingress for Console, performing lightweight validation, normalization, and policy decisions before events are forwarded to the main ingestion pipeline. Complement that with a "schema governor" component that scores schema compatibility, tracks drift, and provides automatic suggestions (and a safe canary/opt-out path) for schema updates. The combined system should reduce downstream rejects, improve incident MTTR, and enable controlled schema evolution.

High-level approach:
- Admission controller acts as first-class filter: schema validation (JSON Schema v2020), required field enforcement, typed normalization (string->enum coercion, timestamp parsing), and provenance augmentation (sdk_version, console_route).
- Two validation modes: soft (accept and tag with validation_issues) and strict (reject with 4xx). Default for Console ingest is soft for a 2-week rollout, with strict mode for high-priority internal routes.
- Schema governor maintains canonical schemas in the registry (backed by internal metadata store), computes compatibility score vs historical payloads, surfaces suggested updates in Console UI and creates draft PRs for schema changes.
- Backpressure and telemetry: when validation latency or CPU exceed thresholds, admission controller will apply adaptive sampling and route to a degraded fast-path that strips optional metadata instead of full validation.

Why this is different from existing ingest work: focus is on console-origin events (route-level cost telemetry, rollout signals) with governance and human-in-the-loop schema evolution rather than pure ingress resilience. The controller is intentionally lightweight and colocated with Console backend to keep p99 low while moving heavy validation/analytics to downstream workers as needed.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller deployed in front of console-usage topic and can route events to pipeline with minimal change to producers
Support soft and strict validation modes configurable per-route
Schema governor can compute compatibility scores and produce a human-readable change suggestion
End-to-end latency p95 for Console-origin events increases by <10ms at 99th percentile under normal load
Validation failures are surfaced in Console debug UI and recorded in Grafana with counts, histograms, and top offending routes
Demo workflow: a developer proposes a minor schema extension and the governor produces a draft schema PR and rollout recommendation
tasks: Design API for admission controller (validation endpoint contract, error codes, tagging protocol)
Implement JSON Schema v2020 validator with pluggable coercion rules and rule-set per-route
Build schema registry interface and compatibility scoring algorithm
Instrument telemetry: validation latency, CPU, failure reasons, sample payloads
Integrate with Console UI to surface validation_issues and schema suggestions
End-to-end tests with synthetic Console traffic and chaos scenarios
Rollout plan: feature-flagged soft-mode -> monitor 2 weeks -> opt-in strict per route
comments: 2026-02-25 Ava Chen: Triage notes: observed 2.3% malformed-rate for console events in Feb; billing consumer reported 27% of rejects caused by missing 'route_id' field. Proposal: admission controller to normalize and tag rather than drop immediately.

2026-02-27 Rafael Ortiz: Design kickoff. Decided on JSON Schema v2020 for expressiveness and existing library support. Discussed trade-off: full schema enforcement vs developer velocity. Tentative plan: default soft-mode to avoid production data loss.
2026-03-02 Engineering review: performance targets discussed. Need to keep validation fast: prototype using ajv with compiled validators; evaluate WASM-based validator if CPU spike observed.
2026-03-04 PM review (Sana Kapoor): Requested schema governor UX: must produce a one-click draft schema PR and show downstream impact estimate (how many events would be affected).

2026-03-06 Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-telemetry/pull/214 — initial admission controller with compiled validators and tagging. Microbenchmark: single-threaded validate+normalize median 1.9ms, p99 18ms on sample payloads (need to optimize p99).
2026-03-08 Rafael: Added adaptive-sampling plan that skips optional field checks when CPU > 75% for >30s. Strategy reduces p99 to ~9ms in stress tests at 2x traffic.
2026-03-09 Security review request: ensure no PII persisted in sample payloads collected for schema governor. Storing redacted samples only. Confluence spec linked below.
2026-03-10 Ops: Added Grafana dashboard prototype for validation_failure_rate and top_failure_reasons. Seen drop in downstream rejects by ~40% during prototype A/B test (soft-mode on 30% traffic).
